games.title: Braid
games.note: Released on Xbox Live Arcade; Jonathan Blow funded much of it himself.

games.title: Super Meat Boy
games.note: Made by two people, Edmund McMillen and Tommy Refenes.

games.title: Fez
games.note: A 2D world you rotate in 3D to reveal hidden paths.

games.title: Shovel Knight
games.note: Funded on Kickstarter in 2013 with over $300,000. Directed by Sean Velasco.

games.title: DuckTales
games.note: Scrooge McDuck bounces on his cane like a pogo stick.

games.title: Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse
games.note: Branching routes and three recruitable partners, including the first appearance of Alucard.

games.title: Cuphead
games.note: Hand-drawn in the style of 1930s cartoons by brothers Chad and Jared Moldenhauer.

games.title: Gunstar Heroes
games.note: Treasure's first game, made by former Konami staff.

games.title: Celeste
games.note: Began as a four-day game jam prototype by Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry on the PICO-8 in 2015.

games.title: TowerFall
games.note: An archery battle game that debuted on the Android-based Ouya console.

games.title: Kero Blaster
games.note: By Daisuke Amaya, the creator of Cave Story.

games.title: The Messenger
games.note: Shifts from 8-bit to 16-bit graphics when you travel in time.

games.title: Ninja Gaiden
games.note: The NES game, known for its cutscenes and steep difficulty; not the 2004 Xbox reboot.

games.title: Spelunky
games.note: First released as freeware; remade for Xbox Live Arcade in 2012.

games.title: Spelunker
games.note: Famous in Japan for its fragile hero, who dies from short falls.

games.title: Rick Dangerous
games.note: An Indiana Jones-style hero in trap-filled caves, from the studio that later made Tomb Raider.

games.title: Flashback
games.note: Directed by Paul Cuisset, with rotoscoped animation traced from video.

games.title: Heart of Darkness
games.note: Eric Chahi's follow-up to Another World.

games.title: Oddworld: Abe's Oddysee
games.note: Abe talks to other characters through a simple command system, GameSpeak. Created by Lorne Lanning.

games.title: Limbo
games.note: Grew from a mood sketch Arnt Jensen drew around 2004 while at IO Interactive.

games.title: Gish
games.note: Co-created by Edmund McMillen, later of Super Meat Boy.

games.title: Planet of Lana
games.note: Director Adam Stjarnljus calls Spirited Away a guiding star for its look.

links.took: Its core platforming, plus castles and a princess who is 'in another castle'.
links.added: Time rewinding and worlds where time bends differently, built into every puzzle.

src.t: The Mushroom Kingdom, citing Jonathan Blow's CVG interview

links.extra: Blow said Super Mario Bros. supplied the core mechanic Braid builds on.

links.took: Rewinding time after a mistake, which Blow felt games like Sands of Time underused.
links.added: Made rewinding the puzzle itself, so death is never final.
links.extra: Blow said he was disenchanted with how rewind was used in games like Sands of Time.

links.took: A model for the solo-made, retro-styled 2D indie hit, per Destructoid's Jonathan Holmes.
links.added: Painted art and time-bending puzzles in place of exploration and shooting.

links.took: World 1-1 style numbering, warp zones and a kidnapped love interest, as a Miyamoto tribute.
links.added: Instant respawns, wall jumps and hundreds of tiny, brutal levels.
links.extra: Edmund McMillen called the game a tribute to Shigeru Miyamoto.

links.took: Brutal difficulty; the developers named Japan's Super Mario Bros. 2 among their NES models.
links.added: Made the pain fair: deaths cost seconds, and replays show every failed attempt at once.

links.took: Punishing NES-era difficulty, named by the developers as part of the game's throwback.
links.added: Short levels with instant retries, so hard games stop feeling cruel.

links.took: Tight jumping through hazard-filled stages, from the hardcore NES classics the team named.
links.added: A meat cube hero, saw blades everywhere and unlockable indie guest characters.

links.took: Confidence: Studio MDHR's founders tried again after Super Meat Boy's 2010 success.
links.added: Hand-drawn 1930s cartoon animation and boss-heavy run-and-gun fights.

links.took: Run-and-gun shooting; the team set out to make a game like Contra.
links.added: Mostly boss battles, drawn and inked by hand like 1930s cartoons.

src.t: Studio MDHR, Road to the IGF, Gamasutra

links.extra: The team said the run-and-gun genre felt lost over the years.

links.took: Frantic two-player run-and-gun action, named alongside Contra as the model.
links.added: Parrying pink objects, weapon loadouts and a big band jazz soundtrack.

src.t: Studio MDHR, Road to the IGF, Gamasutra

links.took: Minimalism and a feeling of lonely isolation, per Phil Fish.
links.added: A 2D world you rotate in 3D, hiding ciphers and secret rooms.

src.t: Gamasutra: How Polytron's Fez was inspired by Ueda's Ico

links.took: Exploration and secrets; Fish said there's 'a LOT of Mario and Zelda' in Fez.
links.added: A world of rotating perspectives, with no combat at all.

src.t: Phil Fish, Road to the IGF, Gamasutra, 2008

links.took: Classic 2D platforming, which Fish named as a core inspiration.
links.added: Turning the world 90 degrees to connect platforms that seemed far apart.

src.t: Phil Fish, Road to the IGF, Gamasutra, 2008

links.took: Environmental puzzles and secrets to decode; Fish cited Myst games as an inspiration.
links.added: Ciphers, codes and secrets so deep that fans worked together to crack them.

links.took: Designer Jonathan Blow and his approach of teaching rules without words.
links.added: A 3D island of line puzzles whose rules you work out on your own.

links.took: The downward thrust, which the designers felt suited a shovel better than a sword.
links.added: Bouncing on enemies with a shovel, plus digging for treasure.

links.took: Themed boss stages: the Order of No Quarter was inspired by the Robot Masters.
links.added: A world map, relics and gold you drop when you die.

links.took: Items with several uses each, which the team modeled on Castlevania III.
links.added: Relics like the Flare Wand and Propeller Dagger, powered by a magic meter.

links.took: Checkpoint design, which the developers said they drew from Dark Souls.
links.added: Breakable checkpoints you can smash for gold, at the cost of safety.

links.took: A smaller influence, per the team; reviewers compared the shovel bounce to Scrooge's pogo cane.
links.added: A bounce that works only on enemies and objects, rooted in Zelda II's downthrust.
links.extra: Velasco said the bounce owes more to Zelda II than to DuckTales.

links.took: Named by the developers as a smaller influence, alongside DuckTales.
links.added: A world map with roaming encounters between Shovel Knight's stages.

links.took: Whip combat, subweapons and Dracula's castle.
links.added: Branching routes and partners you can switch to, including Alucard.

links.took: Its approach to problem-solving; Maddy Thorson called it the game that most inspired Celeste.
links.added: A dash and wall climb up a mountain, with a story about anxiety.

links.took: Lessons from Thorson's own TowerFall, which Noel Berry said carried over.
links.added: A single-player climb with a story and an Assist Mode.

links.took: Cited by Thorson and Berry as an influence on the gameplay.
links.added: Hidden rooms and collectibles tucked into tough, focused climbing chapters.

links.took: Named by Thorson and Berry among the games that shaped Celeste's gameplay.
links.added: Fast respawns and single-screen challenges built around one mid-air dash.

links.took: Cited by Thorson and Berry as a gameplay influence.
links.added: Pixel art paired with a personal story and optional strawberries to chase.

links.took: Level design style; critics saw echoes of Thorson's own Super Mario Maker courses.
links.added: Hundreds of hand-built screens tuned around the dash.

src.t: Shacknews and Kill Screen, via Wikipedia: Celeste

links.took: The modern precision platformer with instant respawns, which Super Meat Boy popularized.
links.added: Gentler framing: assist options, optional strawberries and a personal story.
links.extra: Not a stated influence; many critics compared Celeste's difficulty to Super Meat Boy.

links.took: Its creator, Daisuke 'Pixel' Amaya, and his chunky retro pixel style.
links.added: A short, arcade-like run-and-gun starring a frog company employee.

links.took: Fast ninja platforming; Thierry Boulanger named Ninja Gaiden one of the main inspirations.
links.added: Midway it opens into a metroidvania and jumps between 8-bit and 16-bit eras.

links.took: Named by Thierry Boulanger as a further influence; both play with travel through time.
links.added: Swapped time periods by swapping between 8-bit and 16-bit graphics.

links.took: Platforming feel; Derek Yu called the Super Mario series one of its biggest inspirations.
links.added: Randomly generated caves, permanent death and systems that interact.

links.took: Ruins full of traps and treasure, explored by an archaeologist.
links.added: Short, random levels you replay endlessly instead of one fixed map.

links.took: A fragile cave explorer, ropes and a deep cave to descend.
links.added: Procedural caves, shopkeepers and secrets that change every run.

links.took: An Indiana Jones-style hero, deadly traps and bombs.
links.added: Randomized layouts, so traps can't simply be memorized.

links.took: Credited by Wikipedia as an influence: a freeware 2D game made almost entirely by one person.
links.added: Roguelike randomness in place of a handcrafted, story-driven world.

links.took: Delphine's cinematic, rotoscoped platforming; director Paul Cuisset had co-made Future Wars with Eric Chahi.
links.added: A longer sci-fi story with an inventory, more levels and hand-drawn backdrops.

links.took: Realistic, deliberate running, climbing and ledge-grabbing, which Wikipedia compares to Prince of Persia.
links.added: A sci-fi setting with gunfights, holocubes and a memory-loss plot.
links.extra: Wikipedia notes Flashback's video-capture technique was invented independently of Prince of Persia.

links.took: Eric Chahi's style: a wordless, cinematic platformer with checkpoints, in Another World's vein.
links.added: Pre-rendered backgrounds, CG cutscenes and a boy searching for his dog.

links.took: Deliberate, trap-filled side-scrolling; Lorne Lanning named it among the games he enjoyed most.
links.added: GameSpeak commands to lead fellow slaves to safety.
links.extra: Lanning said film was his key inspiration; among games he named Prince of Persia, Out of This World and Flashback.

links.took: Cinematic drama, which Lanning credited to Out of This World and its peers.
links.added: Possessing enemies with chants, and a satire of factory-farmed food.
links.extra: Out of This World is the North American title of Another World.

links.took: Screen-by-screen cinematic platforming, which Lanning said brought new drama to games.
links.added: Pre-rendered alien worlds and up to 99 Mudokons to rescue.

links.took: Cinematic, animation-driven play; Fumito Ueda listed Flashback among Ico's influences.
links.added: A 3D castle, a companion to lead by the hand, and no on-screen HUD.

links.took: Named by Ueda among Ico's influences; both have you guide helpless characters to safety.
links.added: One companion, Yorda, whom you lead and protect through a castle.

links.took: An artistic, wordless game world; Arnt Jensen said Ico influenced and inspired him greatly.
links.added: A black-and-white 2D forest of deadly traps and physics puzzles.

src.t: Arnt Jensen and Fumito Ueda, Famitsu, 2017

links.extra: Said in a 2017 conversation between Jensen and Ueda, in Japanese.

links.took: Playdead's dark, wordless puzzle-platforming, plus assets reclaimed from Limbo's development.
links.added: Muted 2.5D visuals, mind-control puzzles and a stranger ending.

links.took: The squishiness of Gish's tar-ball hero, cited for the Huddle's animation.
links.added: A mass of bodies you control, rolling and crashing through the final act.

links.took: Wordless puzzle-platforming in a hostile world, cited by director Adam Stjarnljus.
links.added: Hand-painted sci-fi landscapes and a cat-like companion, Mui, who helps with puzzles.

links.took: Puzzle structure: Inside was a major influence on how its puzzles unfold.
links.added: Ghibli-inspired color and a girl-and-creature partnership.

links.took: Dark, side-on puzzle-platforming that critics kept comparing to Limbo.
links.added: Grotesque giants, a child in a yellow raincoat and full 3D depth.
links.extra: Tarsier's David Mervik said they never set out to mimic Playdead: 'They're far better at being Playdead than we are!'

links.took: Platforming know-how: Tarsier worked on LittleBigPlanet's PS Vita version, which it said helped greatly.
links.added: Turned cute physics platforming into a horror story about hunger.
